experiences.title: AI Experimentation with Garment Segmentation
experiences.roleSummary: Sole author. Designed the model-agnostic segmentation interface, ran and hand-triaged the baseline, wrote the referential data validators, and built the FastAPI + React viewer over a PostgreSQL schema.
experiences.summary: Fine-tuning open-source segmentation models to cut clothing out of ordinary photographs while documenting learning and reasoning as it goes.
skills: Designed a model-agnostic segmentation interface returning soft alpha rather than binary masks, so adding a model is one class and one registry entry — the intermediate values are where fur, sheer fabric and open lacework live.

Established a hand-judged baseline across two pretrained models and 22 photographs before any training, to fix the number fine-tuning has to beat and identify which images are worth the cost of labeling.

Identified complementary failure modes between BiRefNet and SegFormer — and that the stronger model passed every flat-lay shot while failing every on-body shot, the actual target domain — which redirected the next round of data collection.
Replaced free-text failure notes with an eleven-term closed vocabulary, making failures countable and surfacing hanger artifacts as the single largest cause at 14 of 44 verdicts.
Built referential validators over three relational CSV tables that catch a truncated identifier three ways at once, rather than relying on duplicated columns agreeing with each other.

Modeled the dataset in PostgreSQL with nanoid primary keys, native enums for closed vocabularies and array columns for multi-valued fields, each enforced by database constraints rather than application-level checks.
Ran the test suite against PostgreSQL in Docker rather than SQLite, using transaction-per-test rollback, to close the dev/prod parity gap that hides constraint and type-coercion bugs.
Verified the suite had teeth by mutation testing — neutering one check constraint failed 28 tests, and the method exposed an earlier security test that passed with its guard deleted.
Built a local FastAPI and React/TypeScript viewer serving 24-megapixel originals downscaled and cached beside each model's cut-out and verdict.
Analyzed licensing across both model code and training data, establishing that SegFormer's NVIDIA non-commercial terms bar it from a commercial product regardless of the repository's own MIT license.
